_comment: V-BRK-029 -- the agent's write path reaches the broker, over mTLS, and nowhere else. Every mutant edits ALL THREE tier copies, so the tier-parity arm can never be the catcher for a conformance defect and each conformance arm has to earn its own verdict. M15 is the single exception and the control for that arm: it drifts exactly one tier. Four mutants (M5, M6, M9, M14) express defects that are invisible to Python alone -- they are only defects relative to Go source or to a module this environment cannot import, which is the whole argument for the check existing at L0. Run with `python3 dev/mutate.py verification/mutants/V-BRK-029.json`.

mutants.why: The certificate is still verified against the CA, but nobody checks it was issued for the host we dialled. Any workload holding a CA-signed certificate can now stand in for the broker, and the write path talks to it. This is the classic half-configured mTLS: it looks verified in every log line.
`CERT_NONE` turns the CA into decoration -- the handshake succeeds against anything presenting anything. mTLS becomes a claim in the design doc.
The server half of mTLS survives and the client half vanishes, so the broker cannot authenticate the pod. 08 §2.3 requires both directions, always.

The exact shape a debugging session leaves behind: verification is configured, and one arm quietly falls back when it fails. Every normal run looks correct; the only run that exercises the fallback is the one where a certificate is wrong -- which is the run that matters.

mutants.why: The agent reads a variable the operator does not render, so the endpoint is empty and every write refuses locally. Nothing in Python notices: the constant is internally consistent. The write path is simply gone, and it reports itself as a wiring fault the operator did not commit.
A plausible API-version edit made on one side. The broker 404s every submission, and a 404 body is not the Response shape, so it surfaces as an opaque transport error rather than as a route mismatch.

A defensible-looking optimisation: one round trip saved per write. The broker's replay guard retires a nonce on use, so the second write of every session is refused as a replay -- and a journal full of replay detections caused by the client is worse than the round trip.

The ten `X-Kube-Agents-*` headers are the broker's tripwire: it refuses the request, journals it, and raises a security event. A client that sets one turns every legitimate write into a recorded attack.

mTLS still succeeds, so the connection is encrypted and mutually authenticated -- and the broker's bearer-token arm has nothing to check. 08 §2.3 requires both, always, because each covers a failure the other does not.
`plan_action` executes. An agent told to preview before committing makes the change instead, and reports it as a preview. There is no worse single-word edit in this module.

The key is computed over an empty identity: well-formed, and identical for every agent in the cluster. The broker derives the identity itself and refuses the mismatch, so the symptom is `idempotency-key-mismatch` on a correctly-formed request -- a wiring fault wearing a tamper-detection label.

The builder's local refusal becomes advisory. Envelopes the builder knows are malformed reach the broker, where they are refused with less context, after a nonce is spent and a journal line is written.

A 403 has no actionId, so the success branch renders `SUBMITTED: decision=accepted` with no detail. The agent then tells a human the cluster changed when it did not. This is the failure the module's docstring names as the only one worse than an error.

mutants.why: One statement in the wrapper, and it is a statement no L0 check can execute -- `platform_mcp_server.py` imports `mcp` and `pydantic`, neither of which exists in the check environment. This is LSN-007 reproduced exactly: built, tested-looking, and unreachable. The catcher is structural for that reason; there is no way to test the statement itself.

THE defect of T8b-4c, in the only shape it can still take after T8b-4d. The value here is `chat`, which is CORRECT and a member -- the point is that a default is the wrong shape whatever it says. `trigger.source` is what splits 06 SS4.1's two autonomy buckets, so a default makes 01 SS7's "how much did the agents decide" a measurement of the default for every caller that did not think about the question. Nothing else can see this: the envelope is legal, the enum mirror agrees, the keys decode, and the transport is right.

mutants.why: The argument that the enum scan is not a special case for `trigger`. `session_requester` supplies `requester.kind` itself, from a literal, exactly the way the trigger source used to be supplied -- and `operator` is not one of 06 SS4.1's requester kinds, so every autonomous action would be a 400.

The vacuity control on the scan, and it has to be behaviour-preserving or the catcher would be whichever unrelated test broke first. The scan reads string literals out of dict literals; hoist the two kinds into a variable and it walks the same dicts, finds zero constants, examines nothing and reports green forever. Every other test stays green, because the module does exactly what it did before. The catcher is the `checked` floor.

The gap a one-statement body leaves open. The MCP tool still delegates, still has one statement, and the schema the model reads still advertises `trigger_source` -- it just never arrives. The model would keep supplying an origin and the client would keep not receiving one. (In production this is a TypeError on the first call; in this environment the MCP module is parsed and never imported, so only the AST arm sees it.)

The same defect one line over, and the reason the forwarding arm compares names rather than counting. Every parameter still reaches the client; two of them arrive as each other. The set-equality half of the arm passes on this, so the `kw.arg == kw.value.id` half has to earn its own verdict.

`plan_action` forwards a constant instead of its own parameter. The envelope is legal, the enum is satisfied, no signature changes and no default exists -- so M16's arm and both static arms pass. The plan and the write it previews are then filed under different origins, which is unreadable afterwards and is counted wrong in 01 SS7. Only driving the request path and reading the trigger back off the wire sees it.

`ref` and `detail` are `omitempty` on `broker.Trigger`, so the builder drops them when empty. Send them always and every envelope carries two blank strings: not a 400, and not visible in any static arm, but `trigger.ref == ""` is a value asserting there was nothing to look at, which is a different claim from having said nothing.

The control for the parity arm, and the only mutant that edits a single tier. Every other mutant here edits all three deliberately, so that byte-parity cannot be the catcher for a conformance defect and the conformance arms have to earn their verdicts. This one proves the parity arm is not itself vacuous.
